description.text: Add stitch keys separated by the step size.
Enable to set convergence automatically from metadata.

Control the size of the smallest level in the Multi-Band blending pyramid. Smaller values of suppression increase the number of pyramid levels, which in turn can help balancing the differences in colour and exposure between images. On the other hand, larger values of suppression result in less pyramid levels, thus the result would be similar to an Alpha blend.

Select the image blending method.
Alpha - Merge images using the alpha channels.
Multi-Band - Merge images at different scales.
Spherical Multi-Band - As above but in spherical domain.
Select which cameras are enabled.
Select a camera combination preset.
Set the consistency between the vectors that align images. Increase consistency to encourage the backward and forward vectors to match.
Set the convergence depth for the scene. Use convergence to align the input images before stitching to reduce any artefacts from the vector warp.
Delete all stitch keys.
Enable stereo stitching using an omni-directional stereo camera model. This needs large overlap between adjacent camera views.

Enable warping of the images using keyed vector computation. Define at least one key frame to start stitching. Use the Cameras tab to select which links are warped. Change the parameters for vector computation in the Vector tab.
Expand blending outside the alpha channels. This can be used to fill areas corresponding to missing views in the image.
Bake out new nodes for the selected export option.

Select the export from the following options: STMaps (split): Create an STMap node with stitch maps STMaps (separate): Create separate STMap nodes with stitch maps Manual STMap Stitch (split): Create a workflow to distort the views through a single split STMap node with stitch maps. Manual STMap Stitch (separate): Create a workflow to distort the original inputs through STMap nodes with stitch maps. PPass (split): Create an STMap node with ppass maps PPass (separate): Create separate STMap nodes with ppass maps Manual PPass Stitch (split): Create a workflow to distort the views through a single split STMap node with ppass maps. Manual PPass Stitch (separate): Create a workflow to distort the original inputs through STMap nodes with ppass maps.
Set the eye distance for the left and right views. This defines the Interpupillary Distance (IPD) for the stitch. Use the same units as the rig size defined in the upstream CameraSolver node.

Set the type of eye separation falloff model.
None - Keep the same eye separation along all latitude values.
Linear - Set a linear decay starting at the given start falloff angle value.
Cosine - Set a cosine decay according to the given exponent.
Sigmoid - Set a sigmoid decay minimising the falloff area at the poles.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.
Import stitch keys from another CaraVR node. Importing will delete any currently defined key.

Set the projection for the input camera views. Use 'Source' to project inputs to the panorama using the metadata from C_CameraSolver. Use 'Latlong' for inputs that have already been projected to the output panorama.

Set the number of frames between adjacent analysis keys. The image alignment is interpolated between the analysis keys. Reduce the frame separation to align content where there are rapid changes in depth. Increase the frame separation to improve temporal stability in the stitch.
Set the output left view for the stereo stitch.
Select which images are linked together, which will cause them to be warped to become aligned.

Set the rate of fall-off for the eye separation towards the poles. This defines the exponent of a cosine function. Set the exponent to one to get a smooth merging of depth at the poles between left and right view. Reduce the exponent to shift the transition in depth toward the poles. Set the falloff to zero to prevent pole merging.
Set the starting angle for linear fall-off in the eye separation towards the poles. Increase the angle to shift the start point for fall-off towards the poles. Set this to 90 to prevent pole merging.
Set the strength in matching images. Increase to force image alignment, decrease to make the vectors smoother.
Sets the number of frames on either side of each key to use in temporal averaging. Increase for temporally smoother vectors, but also significantly longer computation time.

Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.
Controls the density of the vector field. Increase for higher resolution vectors, but also longer computation time.
Set the number of warps in the vector calculation. Increase to handle large image displacements, but with a longer computation time.

description.plain_text: C_Stitcher 2.1v5: Stitch camera images to produce a seamless panorama. Input: Set the projection type for the input views. The projection for the source footage is defined by the metadata from an upstream C_CameraSolver node. Stitch: Set the stitch options. Override the cameras to define the inputs that are used in the stitch and the links that are warped for alignment. Enable stereo stitching to generate a left/right stereoscopic panorama. The links for stitching and the output view for each camera are defined by C_CameraSolver. Keying: Set analysis keys to define where vectors are calculated to align linked images. Place analysis keys where there are depth changes in the overlap between images. Output: Set the convergence depth for the panorama before stitching. Use this to align images at a selected depth before vector warping. Export: Export STMaps for the image stitch to perform manual corrections on the STMap without introducing an extra filter hit.
description.text:
C_Stitcher 2.1v5: Stitch camera images to produce a seamless panorama.

Input: Set the projection type for the input views. The projection for the source footage is defined by the metadata from an upstream C_CameraSolver node.

Stitch: Set the stitch options. Override the cameras to define the inputs that are used in the stitch and the links that are warped for alignment. Enable stereo stitching to generate a left/right stereoscopic panorama. The links for stitching and the output view for each camera are defined by C_CameraSolver.

Keying: Set analysis keys to define where vectors are calculated to align linked images. Place analysis keys where there are depth changes in the overlap between images.

Output: Set the convergence depth for the panorama before stitching. Use this to align images at a selected depth before vector warping.

Export: Export STMaps for the image stitch to perform manual corrections on the STMap without introducing an extra filter hit.
